articles.title: Venezuela Declares National Rabies Quarantine After Six Deaths in 2026
articles.description: Venezuela has declared a national epidemiological quarantine following six confirmed rabies deaths in 2026. The Ministry of Health reported the death of a 14-year-old in the Sifontes municipality of Bolívar state due to bat exposure. In Zulia state, five fatalities were attributed to stray dog attacks, claiming the lives of a 68-year-old woman, a 44-year-old man, a 20-year-old man, and two children aged 6 and 14. Laboratory data from the 42nd epidemiological week of 2026 in Zulia state show that 154 of 219 animal brain tissue samples tested positive, a positivity rate of 70.32%. Of these, 128 cases were confirmed in stray dogs, while 19 were found in cats. Wild bats carrying the forest strain of the virus were also identified. The outbreak has affected nine municipalities in Zulia. The highest concentrations are in the Caracabo agglomeration with 77 foci, followed by San Francisco (23), Mara (16), and Lagunillas (12). Nationally, reported suspicious bites reached 42,363, a 25.9% increase over 2025 figures. During the 42nd week alone, health facilities recorded 967 reports of animal bites.
